sources.note: To verify: the standard library reference notes that items in s * n 'are not copied; they are referenced multiple times', with the [[]] * 3 example and the list comprehension fix. writeup.question: For the box office: why one booking sold a whole column, what you changed, and how you know.

parts.label: Why
parts.criteria: Multiplying a list does not copy its items: [["free"] * 12] * 8 holds 8 references to one inner list, so seats[r][s] = "sold" changes what every row shows. Not an index or data error.
parts.modelAnswer: All eight rows were one list object.

parts.label: What you changed
parts.criteria: Build each row anew with a comprehension. Copying the outer list, or repeating one prebuilt row in a comprehension, keeps the rows shared. Resetting the map destroys real bookings.
parts.modelAnswer: [["free"] * SEATS for _ in range(ROWS)]; the map rebuilt from the ticket log.

parts.label: How you know
parts.criteria: After the last change, a test books one seat and finds one seat sold, and checks seats[0] is not seats[1].

right.headline: Good: eight rows, eight lists
right.body: * repeats references, not copies. A comprehension evaluates its expression once per row, so each row is a new list, and the identity test proves it.

wrongSent.headline: Still shared
wrongSent.body: Copying the outer list copies the references; a comprehension that repeats one prebuilt row repeats the reference. The inner list must be created inside the comprehension.

scoring.modelReasoning: One booking marking a whole column means the rows are not separate. [["free"] * 12] * 8 builds one inner list and 8 references to it, so seats[r][s] = "sold" shows in every row; seats[0] is seats[1] is True. list(...) copies only the outer list, and [row for _ in range(8)] repeats one prebuilt row. A comprehension that creates the inner list each time, [["free"] * 12 for _ in range(8)], gives 8 lists. Test one booking and row identity, then rebuild tonight's map from the ticket log rather than resetting real bookings.
